content: A formula unit in chemistry refers to the simplest empirical formula of an ionic or covalent network solid compound, which is used as a discrete entity for stoichiometric calculations. It represents the smallest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound. For example, sodium chloride (NaCl) and potassium oxide (K₂O) are ionic compounds, while silicon dioxide (SiO₂) and carbon (in the forms of diamond or graphite) are examples of covalent network solids. Ionic compounds do not exist as distinct molecules; instead, the formula unit represents the lowest reduced ratio of ions within the compound. Essentially, a formula unit specifies the types and numbers of atoms in the smallest representative unit of a given substance.
